title: Partitioning of net CO2 exchanges at the city-atmosphere interface into biotic and abiotic components
author: Lee, Hong, et al.

steps.title: Prepare eddy covariance dataset
steps.instruction: Collect continuous eddy covariance (EC) measurements at the site and gather ancillary data required for footprint analysis (traffic volumes, vegetation index such as EVI, and high‑resolution land‑cover map).

steps.title: Compute 30‑min CO₂ flux
steps.instruction: Use EddyPro software (version 6.2.0, LI‑COR, USA) to calculate 30‑minute CO₂ fluxes from raw 10 Hz sampled data, then apply the standard quality‑control procedure described in reference [3] and its cited works.

steps.title: Generate footprint climatology
steps.instruction: Run the footprint model of Hsieh et al. [2] with the following inputs: (a) atmospheric stability estimated from the EC data, (b) aerodynamic roughness parameters (roughness length and zero‑plane displacement height) derived from digital surface and terrain models at 1 × 1 m² resolution supplied by the National Geographic Information Institute, and (c) a 1 m‑resolution land‑cover map obtained from the Environmental Geographic Information Service (https://egis.me.go.kr).

steps.title: Calculate footprint‑weighted land‑cover fractions (λ)
steps.instruction: Overlay each footprint on the land‑cover map and sum the footprint‑weighted fractions of each class (tree, grass, building, road, impervious, water, bare soil, other) to obtain λ for the whole footprint and λ_R for the road class.

steps.title: Obtain traffic volume data
steps.instruction: Retrieve hourly traffic volume counts from the nearest road monitoring station (e.g., https://topis.seoul.go.kr). In the example case the daily traffic volume is approximately 100 000 vehicles d⁻¹ for Seoul Forest Park and ≈10 000 vehicles d⁻¹ for the KUOM site.

steps.title: Model vehicle emissions (ER)

steps.title: Model building emissions (EB)

steps.title: Select temporal subsets for partitioning
steps.instruction: Identify periods in the FC time series where one or more components of Eq. (1) are negligible, following the logic of MM2017: e.g., wintertime with low traffic for EB‑only, or periods with high traffic for ER estimation, leaf‑off periods for RE, etc. Adjust the subset criteria to the characteristics of the study site.

steps.title: Estimate ecosystem respiration (RE)
steps.instruction: Model RE by fitting nighttime FC (when photosynthesis is absent) against air or soil temperature, using the same approach applied in natural canopies and croplands (e.g., reference [15]).

steps.title: Calculate gross primary production (P)
steps.instruction: Compute P for each time step as P = FC – RE – ER – EB, using the previously derived RE, ER, and EB values.

steps.title: Assemble final flux partition
steps.instruction: Combine the four components (RE, ER, EB, P) to obtain the full partitioned urban CO₂ budget according to Eq. (1): FC = RE – P + ER + EB.
